Start a blend stack

Source: R/blend.R
rvt_stack.Rd

The background layer a stack is built on. Only needed when the background itself needs a range or invert; otherwise pipe the raster straight into rvt_blend(), which starts a stack for you.

Usage

rvt_stack(base, range = NULL, invert = FALSE)

Arguments

base

path to the background raster

range

c(lo, hi) to stretch over, or NULL (default) for the raster's own minimum and maximum. See rvt_range().

invert

flip the layer after stretching, so high reads dark

Value

an rvt_stack

See also

rvt_blend() to add layers, rvt_render() to write the result

Examples

dem <- system.file("extdata", "dtm1.tif", package = "rvtr")
dem |> rvt_hillshade() |> rvt_stack(range = c(0, 1))
#> <rvt_stack> 1 layer, bottom to top
#>   1. file223ed3c2e74.tif          (background) opacity 1.00  range 0-1
#> Renders at 1000 x 1000, 1 m. Not a raster yet - call rvt_render() to write it.
